nodes.summary: The BK inequality for decreasing events: under the product Bernoulli(`p`) measure on a finite set, `P_p(A □ B) ≤ P_p(A) * P_p(B)` for decreasing `A, B`.
nodes.title: BK inequality for decreasing events

nodes.summary: The BK inequality for two decreasing events under a product probability weight, obtained from `StatMech.bk_wprob_general` by flipping all coordinates.
nodes.title: BK inequality for decreasing events under product weights

nodes.summary: The configuration with every coordinate flipped, `x ↦ !(ω x)`.
nodes.title: Flipping every coordinate of a configuration

nodes.summary: Flipping all coordinates, as an involutive equivalence of `ConfigSpace E`.
nodes.title: Coordinate flip as an involutive equivalence

nodes.summary: Reimer's inequality `P_p(A □ B) ≤ P_p(A) * P_p(B)` for all events under the product Bernoulli measure on a finite set, assuming `ReimerWprobCore`.
nodes.title: Reimer's inequality for Bernoulli measures, assuming the core case

nodes.summary: Reimer's inequality (the van den Berg–Kesten conjecture, proved by Reimer 2000) for product probability weights on `Fin n`: for every `n`, every weight `φ` with `φ ≥ 0` and `φ i false + φ i true = 1`, and all events `A, B`, `wprob φ (A □ B) ≤ wprob φ A * wprob φ B`.
nodes.title: Reimer's inequality

nodes.summary: Reimer's inequality for product probability weights on any finite set, assuming `ReimerWprobCore`.
nodes.title: Reimer's inequality for product weights, assuming the core case

nodes.summary: Reimer's inequality on the one-point configuration space `ConfigSpace (Fin 0)`.
nodes.title: Reimer's inequality on the one-point configuration space

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
